moline-moline-1910-08-15.A1:
MOLINE IS CLOSE TO A RACE CLASH
Building Occupied by Negroes
Surrounded by Mob of Men
at Midnight.
MANY OF THEM ARE ARMED
Uprising Follows Report That White Girl Had Been Pursued and Her Friends Beaten.
Moline narrowly averted a race clash last night following a report that a white girl had been pursued by two negroes and that the latter had beaten two young men who had interfered to protect the girl. Between 11 and 12 o'clock 50 men, some of them mounted, and the majority of them armed, gathered about the Looker building, at Twenty-fourth avenue and Fifteenth street, prepared to "regulate" the nirst negro who showed his head. The Looker building several years ago was abandoned for business purposes and was converted into a dwelling. It is a large three-story structure, and it is said that fully 100 negroes are making their abode there at present.

Police Disperse Mob.

Various insults to white people have been reported in the neighborhood, and the people of that section of the city have repeatedly expressed their indignation by verbal threats of prosecution, and the feeling crystalized last night following the rumored attack upon a white girl. Windows of the building were smashed with rocks last night, but not a single occupant of the place appeared. Three police officers were soon on the scene, and succeeded in dispersing the mob before any further harm had been done.
moline-moline-1910-08-15.A2:
MOLINE
Bradley Goes to Watertown.—After spending a week at the county jail, where he begged to be sent to escape the fury of the whites whom he claimed were about to lynch him, Tom Bradely, aged 60 years, one of the pioneer colored residents of the city was committed to the insane hospital at Watertown, following a hearing before the insanity commission at Rock Island. It is now rumored that Bradley, who resides in the "Incubator," received advance notice of the impending clash between the whites and the blacks and that it was because he feared violence at the hands of the whites of the vicinity that he begged to be sent to jail. Bradley has been a resident of this city for the past 40 years and is a local character. It is not thought that any injury would have been done him had he remained at the "Incubator," as he was generally liked by the white people about the city. Bradley, however, had been acting queerly for months and it was for that reason that the police discredited his tale of an impending race riot.

Goes on Cruise.—Moline members of the Illinois Naval Reserves to the number of 50 will leave here tonight over the Milwaukee road for Chicago on their annual cruise along the great lakes. The men will board the Nashville with the second division of Chicago. The cruise this year will extend to Detroit and will last until Aug. 29. Three members of the local division are now aboard the Nashville on a squadron cruise. Lieutenant George Kemmerling will not accompany his men this year, owing to stress of business. He will attend to the loading and unloading and will accompany them as far as Chicago. A few of the men will not make the trip this summer because of sickness and business.

Driver Fined.—Gust Abrahamson, driver for Shoecraft & Son Co., a commission firm in Davenport, was fined $6.80 this afternoon for driving on the asphalt with an overloaded wagon. The tires were two and one-quarter inches wide and the load weighed 6390 pounds.

Candidate for Bartenders' President.—Al Olson of this city is preparing to wage an aggressive battle for the presidency of the Illinois state branch of the International Bartenders' league at the convention next month. The meeting will be held in Bloomington on the 20th and it is expected that the attendance will be a record breaker.

Burglars Foiled In Attempt.—Burglaries made an unsuccessful attempt Thursday night to enter the clothing store owned by Coleman & Schultz and it is thought that they were frightened away while at work. From appearances the proprietors believe that amateurs tried to break into the place. A screen which had been removed from a rear window was what attracted his attention. The screen had been pried out of place. Marks on the window casing gave evidence that an attempt had been made to force the window. A harrow tooth was found on the ground near the window, and it is thought that it was dropped by burglars when they made a hurried getaway.
moline-moline-1910-08-15.A3: MOLINE. Ill.—Hundred white residents of South Moline are seeking five negroes, who attacked a white girl; police already have rescued several negroes from lynching by the mob.
moline-moline-1910-08-15.A4:
WHITE IS KILLED BY PAIR NEGROES
Edward Wyman Is Slain Within Eighteen Feet of His Home in Moline.
HOLDUP IS ATTEMPTED
Intended Victim Hurls Bucket of Beer in Faces of Bandits, One of Whom Shoots—Both Escape.
Edward Wyman was shot down within eighteen feet of his home in Moline at 10:30 Saturday night when he refused the command of two negro bandits to deliver over his money to them. Wyman died at 12:05 at the Moline city hospital. One shot was fired, the bullet puncturing Wyman's intestines. He remained conscious until the end, and gave the police authorities the details of the tragedy, although unable to describe his assailants further than to say that they were both negroes. Wyman's home is at Third avenue and Twenty-third street. He was on his way from a neighboring saloon with a bucket of beer, when he was halted by the pair of blacks. One of them placed a revolver in front of Mr. Wyman's face and ordered that he hold up his hands; that his money was wanted.

Dashes Beer in Faces.

The command was refused, and after Wyman had told the fellows what he thought of them he dashed the contents of the bucket in their faces. The taller of the two negroes held the revolver. Lowering it from Wyman's face when the beer was thrown, he held the weapon close to the abdomen of his victim and fired.

Wyman fell to the walk, and when he made an outcry the blacks fled. No one witnessed the shooting save the negroes and their victim. Neighbors heard the cries of Wyman, who crawled to the porch of his home, where he was lying when a physician and police officers arrived shortly after the shooting. He was removed to the hospital.

City Overrun by Negroes. At 1 o'clock Sunday morning a strange negro was arrested in East Moline, but there was no evidence on which to hold him, and he was released. Moline is overrun by negroes who have been imported by contractors having large building jobs in that city and vicinity.
